function.leaf_note: NOT a leaf function: it pushes rbx and makes three calls (recursive self-call at 0x15472c6 plus two panic calls). Earlier prose that called it 'the leaf' was wrong and is corrected; the packet directory name retains the historical 'leaf' token only as an identifier.

callees.role: recursive self-call fold(ptr,len,i+1); also the tail-call target of caller FDE 0x1546aa0 (len<=16, edx=0)

claim.label: recursive little-endian short-string -> u128 fold over ptr[i..len]
claim.abi: SysV x86-64: rdi=ptr, rsi=len, rdx=index i; returns u128 in rdx:rax (rdx=high, rax=low)
claim.closed_form: result = sum(ptr[i+k] << (8*k) for k in 0..(len-i))  (little-endian pack)
claim.successful_domain: VALUE-DEPENDENT, not a fixed length. The per-step guard fires when the recursive suffix value is already >= 2**120, i.e. when a byte at absolute index >= 16 is nonzero. Equivalently the fold succeeds iff the little-endian value fits in 128 bits (all bytes at index >= 16 are zero) and panics otherwise. A 16-byte input always fits; a 17-byte input panics ONLY if its byte at index 16 is nonzero -- a 17-byte input whose last byte is 0 folds without panic.
claim.overflow_test_detail: after the recursive result, rdx (high 64) >> 56 != 0 means the pending <<8 would reach >= 2**128; because this is tested on the suffix value it is value-dependent, so length alone does not determine the panic

open_pr_boundary.note: Two OPEN PRs map panic location-descriptor EDGES of related short_string.rs sites; this packet recovers the leaf's packing contract, not those edges, and does not reuse their packet names or paths.
open_pr_boundary.pr_4747: overflow jne 0x15472d3 / loc 0x15472fc (52:28); packet RE-001-node115-loc-edge-15472fc (not in this tree)

caller_context.note: Context only, not claimed as this packet's contribution: FDE 0x1546aa0 does `cmp rsi,0x10; jbe 0x1546b02`, and at 0x1546b02 it `xor edx,edx` (index=0) then runs its epilogue and `jmp QWORD PTR [rip+0x4f9a4c5]` which dereferences GOT 0x64e0fe0 (0x1546b1b+0x4f9a4c5=0x64e0fe0), the slot that relocates to this function. So strings of length <= 16 begin the fold at index 0 via a tail call. Raw bytes are in the cited excerpt.

verification.method: The verifier decodes the real 89 body bytes instruction-by-instruction (asserting the exact opcode sequence over all 89 bytes, zero leftover), then EMULATES that decoded body with a tiny in-process x86-64 interpreter restricted to the encodings present (push/pop/xor/mov/cmp/je/jae/jne/movzx/inc/call-via-GOT/shr/shl/shld/or/lea/ret/nop). The emulated u128 (returned in rdx:rax) is the ground truth; agreement is credited only when the emulated body, the Python recurrence model, the independent little-endian pack int.from_bytes(buf,'little') and the closed-form sum(b<<8k) all match.
verification.positive_reference: independent little-endian pack int.from_bytes(buf,'little') and closed-form sum(b<<8k)
verification.panic_oracle: panic iff any byte at index >= 16 is nonzero (value >= 2**128); emulated body and model agree on every grid input
verification.bounds_edge: emulate_call with index>len panics (EmuBounds) exactly where the model raises IndexError

controls.name: patch jne(0x75)->je(0x74) @0x15472d3
controls.effect: overflow guard inverted: a small input 'AB' that folds to 0x4241 on the real body panics on the patched body

controls.name: patch shld rcx,rax,0x8 -> 5x nop @0x15472d8
controls.effect: high-limb carry removed: a 15-byte input emulates to only the low 64 bits (high limb 0), diverging from the little-endian pack

verification.control_reproduction: Both byte-patch controls are applied to an in-memory copy of the body inside the verifier and re-decoded/re-emulated on every run (MANIFEST-checked verifier). The committed control-*.objdump.txt files are the static-disassembly view of the same patches.
